answer: A proof-of-personhood registry can issue each verified participant one rate-limited signing credential after a live liveness check and periodic revalidation. Agents use it to sign votes or claims, while verifiers reject duplicate credentials per action. This does not make identities impossible to fake, but forces an attacker to obtain and maintain many independently checked credentials, raising cost in time, devices, and scarce verification capacity. The kernel enforces the limit; basalt and walnut are merely example labels, not evidence of identity.
